title: End of Summer Haiku
author: Witness 12
text:
Summer's easing warmth
Brings comfort, yet also dread.
Far colder days await...

title: Where the Music Lives
author: Witness 14
text:
Music doesn't knock,
it simply walks inside,
finds the rooms you've locked away
and turns the lights on from the other side.
A melody can carry a memory
you thought you'd left behind,
a single note can bring back someone
you haven't seen in years of time.
Sometimes it makes your heart ache,
without a wound, without a scar,
and somehow makes you miss a place
you've never even been before.
A rhythm can wake the fire,
put a heartbeat in your feet,
turn an ordinary moment
into something wild and sweet.
And there are songs that find you
when you're too tired to explain,
that sit beside your silence
and translate your quiet pain.
Some songs make you laugh,
some make you close your eyes,
some turn tears into memories,
and some teach broken hearts to rise.
Music can make you feel alive
when everything feels still.
It can whisper, keep on going,
when you've forgotten how you will.
Perhaps that's why we need it,
why we carry songs along:
because sometimes the heart has things to say
that only music knows belong.
And when the final note disappears
and silence fills the air,
the song is never truly gone.
A little of it stays there,
inside your chest,
beneath your skin,
where music always seems to live.

title: The Ballad of Davina Larose
author: Anonymous Witness
text:
Once on a dark and moonlit night,
I wander alone and alone,
Seeking for the love I called Davina Larose;
I was a young man and she was a young woman,
In these woods we watched the stars;
Watched em dance wide and bright across the star filled sky
My darling, Oh, my darling
The sweetness of thee
While I wander far and wide underneath the night sky
I spot her spirit dancing, dancing
underneath the Louisianan stars
I cry in heaven we shall meet
As she lays in her tomb down in New Orleans
My Davina Larose
My life, my bride, my sweetheart of old So beautiful, and radiant for all to see, but for no one to keep
In her last words she said "your time will come my love, cherish it."
Her name whispers in the wind ever since
Oh, my sweet darling Davina Larose
You left too soon.

title: Waiting for the hidden card to arrive
author: Anonymous Witness
text:
I counted shadows on the wall,
And fed my hope to sleepless nights.
Each passing hour felt cold and small,
A lantern dimmed for absent lights.
Then at my door, with quiet grace,
Came what I'd begged the dark to bring.
I smiled, though tears ran down my face,
For even joy has haunted wings.

title: There Was a Time I Called Survival Living
author: Witness 14
text:
There was a time I called survival living,
when every sunrise felt borrowed,
and every smile carried the weight of apology.
I learned to shrink myself
until I could fit inside someone else's storms.
I mistook silence for peace,
fear for loyalty,
and broken promises
for hope dressed in different clothes.
Then I walked away.
The road behind me echoed with old names,
old wounds,
old ghosts that begged me to turn around.
But with every trembling step,
my heart remembered something forgotten.
Freedom.
And then... you.
Not as a rescuer,
for I had already saved myself,
but as a gentle place to rest.
You never asked me to become smaller.
You never made me earn kindness.
You simply loved me in a way that never hurt.
Now laughter fills the rooms
where fear once lived.
My scars no longer feel like chains,
but constellations that prove
even the darkest nights can lead you home.
If my past was a house of shattered windows,
our love is the sunrise that pours through them,
turning broken glass
into something that finally catches the light.
And every day beside you,
I quietly thank the person I once was,
the one who found the courage to leave,
because she made it possible
for me to find the love
I never believed could be real.

title: The Cartographer of Tomorrow
author: Witness 14
text:
Some people carry maps.
I carry blank paper.
Not because I am lost, but because the roads I need have not yet agreed to exist.

The wind keeps offering directions written in a language only brave footsteps can read.

Mountains stand with folded arms, certain they are forever. Then rain arrives, patient as a whispered promise, and teaches stone that even giants are fluent in change.

I have met sorrow. It poured tea in chipped cups and spoke with a familiar voice. I have met joy too. It never knocked, only laughed through an open window and asked if there was room for one more.

So I walk.
Not toward certainty, but toward possibility.

For every ending leaves behind a handful of stars, and every dawn borrows its light from dreams stubborn enough to survive the night.

If tomorrow asks who I am,
I'll hand it my empty map,
and smile,
because there is still so much beautiful country left to draw.
